data.title: Intensity and retention time prediction improves the rescoring of protein-nucleic acid cross-links
data.projectDescription: Rescoring of protein-RNA cross-links using retention time and intensity prediction.
data.sampleProcessingProtocol:
Escherichia coli BL21 DE3 cells were grown in LB medium to OD600 ≈ 0.6. 15 mL of cell culture (corresponding to 7 x 109 cells) were used as starting material per biological replicate for UV and chemical crosslinking. UV, DEB and NM crosslinking were performed in LB medium. Cells were UV crosslinked in glass petri dishes (d = 12 cm, vol. cell suspension ≈ 11, ht. cell suspension ≈ 1 mm) for 10 min at a 2 cm distance from four parallel UVC Germicidal T5 lamps (Sylvania; G8W; 0000501; λ=254 nm) as part of an in-house built crosslinking apparatus. DEB crosslinking was performed using 50 mM DEB for 10 min, 37°C, 300 rpm. NM crosslinking was performed with 1 mM NM for 10 min, 37°C, 300 rpm. DEB and NM crosslinking reactions were quenched with final 50 mM Tris/HCl pH 7.5 and incubation for 5 min, RT, 300 rpm. FA crosslinking was performed in PBS at 1% [v/v] FA for 10 min, 37°C, 300 rpm, followed by quenching using 400 mM Tris/HCl pH 7.5 for 10 min, RT, 300 rpm. Cells were pelleted at 3000xg for 10 min and washed with ice-cold PBS. Cell pellets were either fractionated (see below) or stored at -80 °C until further use. For UV, DEB and NM crosslinked cells, S30/S100 fractionation by ultracentrifugation was performed as described in 45.  UV, DEB and NM crosslinked S30 and S100 fractions were EtOH precipitated as described above, pellets were washed and dissolved in Pellets were dissolved in 8 M urea, 50 mM Tris/HCl pH 7.5 in a sonication bath, 3 min. LysC (Promega; V1671) was added at a 1:100 enzyme-to-protein ratio, following incubation at 30°C, ON, 300 rpm. Urea concentration was diluted to 1 M using 50 mM Tris/HCl pH 7.5. Trypsin was added at a 1:50 enzyme-to-protein ratio, following incubation ON, 30°C, 300 rpm. Samples were EtOH precipitated as described above and dissolved in 4 M urea, 50 mM Tris/HCl pH 7.5 in a sonication bath, 3 min. Urea concentration was diluted to 1 M using 50 mM Tris/HCl pH 7.5 and 1mM MgCl2, 625 U Pierce™ Universal nuclease, 250 U nuclease P1 were added, following incubation for 3 h, 37°C, 300 rpm. Trypsin was added at a 1:100 enzyme-to-protein ratio, following incubation ON, 37°C, 300 rpm. Samples were acidified with 10% [v/v] formic acid (FA) to pH 3-4 and 2.5% [v/v] ACN was added. Sample clean-up was performed using C18 stage tips (Harvard Apparatus; 74-4107) according to manufacturer’s instructions. Briefly, columns were equilibrated with each 400 μL of 100% ACN; 50% [v/v] ACN, 0.1% [v/v] FA; and three times 0.1% [v/v] FA. Samples were loaded twice and washed three times with 5% [v/v] ACN, 0.1% [v/v] FA. Elution was performed using 200 μL of each 50% [v/v] ACN, 0.1% [v/v] FA and 80% [v/v] ACN, 0.1% [v/v] FA. All centrifugation steps were performed for 1 min at 800xg. Peptides were dried in a speed vac concentrator. Enrichment of crosslinked peptide-(oligo)nucleotides was performed using TiO2 as described in 19 using Titansphere TiO2 10 nm beads (GL Sciences; 5020-75010). Buffer A contained 5% [v/v] glycerol in buffer B; buffer B contained 60% [v/v] ACN, 5% [v/v] trifluoroacetic acid (TFA); buffer B2 contained 60% [v/v] ACN and 0.1% [v/v] TFA; buffer C contained 0.3 M NH4OH, pH 10.5. Columns were self-packed by adding 3 mg TiO2 beads in 100 % MeOH to p200 pipette tips equipped with a coffee filter tip. Columns were equilibrated with 60 μL of each 100% MeOH, buffer B and buffer A. Dried samples were dissolved in 60 μL buffer A and loaded twice and washed three times with buffer A, three times with buffer B and once with buffer B2. Elution was performed in three steps of each adding 40 μL buffer C. Elution tubes contained 20 μL of 10% [v/v] FA for pH neutralization. All centrifugation steps were performed for 2-3 min at 800xg. Eluted crosslinked peptide-(oligo)nucleotides were dried in a speed vac concentrator and subjected to LC-MS/MS measurements. Eluted crosslinked peptide-(oligo)nucleotides were dried in a speed vac and dissolved in 35 µL 10 mM NH4OH pH 10, 5% [v/v] CAN for high pH reversed phase fractionation. Crosslinked peptides were loaded onto an Xbridge C18 column (Waters; 186003128) using an Agilent 1100 series chromatography system. The column was operated at a flow rate of 60 µl/min with a buffer system consisting of 10 mM NH4OH pH 10 (buffer A) and 10 mM NH4OH pH10, 80% [v/v] ACN (buffer B). The column was equilibrated with 5% buffer B and developed over 64 min using the following gradient: 5% buffer B (0-7 min), 8-30% buffer B (8-42 min), 30-50% buffer B (43-50 min), 90-95% buffer B (51-56 min), 5% buffer B (57-64 min). The first 6 min were collected as one flow-through fraction, followed by 48 x 1 min fractions, which were reduced to 12 fractions by concatenated pooling. Fractions were dissolved in MS buffer for LC-MS/MS measurements. For this study, only data from fractions 6-10 were used.
UV, DEB and NM crosslinked peptide-(oligo)nucleotide E. coli samples were dissolved in 2% [v/v] ACN 0.1% [v/v] TFA and injected onto a C18 PepMap100-trapping column (0.3 x 5 mm, 5 μm, Thermo Scientific) connected to an in-house packed C18 analytical column (75 μm x 300 mm; Reprosil-Pur 120C18-AQ, 1.9 μm, Dr Maisch GmbH). Columns were equilibrated using 8% buffer A (0.1% [v/v] formic acid (FA)), 2% buffer B (80% [v/v] ACN, 0.1% [v/v] FA). Liquid chromatography was performed using an UltiMate-3000 RSLC nanosystem (Thermo Scientific). Purified, crosslinked E. coli ribosome samples were analysed for 58 min using a linear gradient (10% to 45% buffer B (80% [v/v] ACN, 0.1% [v/v] FA in 44 min) followed by a 4.8 min washing step at 90% of buffer B. Eluting peptides were analysed on an Orbitrap Exploris 480 instrument (Thermo Scientific). The following MS settings were used for purified, crosslinked E. coli ribosome samples: MS1 scan range, 350–1600 m/z; MS1 resolution, 120,000 FWHM; AGC target MS1, 1E6; maximum injection time MS1, 60 ms; isolation window, 1.6 m/z; collision energy, 30%; charge states, 2+ to 6+; dynamic exclusion, 9 s; Top 20 most abundant precursors were selected for fragmentation; MS2 resolution, 30,000, AGC target MS2, 1e5; maximum injection time MS2, 120 ms.
data.dataProcessingProtocol: We used the protein-RNA crosslinking search engine NuXL (v. 2023-02-01, publication in progress) to generate cross-link identifications used in this study. The search engine parameters across collected different protocol datasets are given in the supplementary material. To derive accurate retention times of cross-linked peptides, we provided high-confidence CSMs (q < 0.01) as input to the OpenMS FeatureFinderIdentification algorithm. The retention time at the apex of the extracted elution profiles was subsequently used as retention time used in the training.
